subject: Accounting
title: Auditor Independence
description: A short lesson to help you apply Auditor Independence.

hook.text: Arthur Andersen earned more from consulting for Enron than from auditing it. Independence died.

buildup.text: When auditors depend on a client for big fees, the temptation to overlook problems grows.

discovery.text: Post-scandal rules now limit what consulting services auditors can sell to their audit clients.

twist.text: Despite reforms, the Big Four still earn more from consulting than auditing. The tension persists.

climax.text: True independence requires more than rules—it demands a culture that prizes integrity over fees.

punchline.text: You can't guard the vault and sell the keys.

quiz.question: Why is auditor independence important?
options: Auditors must not depend on clients for non-audit fees

details.summary: Auditor independence means external auditors must have no financial, personal, or business relationships that could bias their professional judgment. This topic explains independence requirements, why they matter, and how scandals exposed failures in maintaining them.
details.whyItMatters: An audit provides assurance only if the auditor has no incentive to please the client. Loss of independence turns auditing from a safeguard into a rubber stamp.
takeaways: Independence in fact means the auditor is unbiased; independence in appearance means outsiders see no bias
Pre-SOX, audit firms often earned more from consulting than auditing the same client
Sarbanes-Oxley banned most non-audit services by a company's external auditor

faq.question: Why is auditor independence important?
faq.answer: Auditor independence ensures that the auditor's opinion on financial statements is unbiased and credible. If auditors have financial or personal ties to the client, they may be reluctant to report problems—rendering the audit meaningless for investors and regulators.

faq.question: How does Sarbanes-Oxley protect auditor independence?
faq.answer: SOX prohibits audit firms from providing most consulting services to audit clients, requires mandatory rotation of lead audit partners every five years, bans auditors from auditing companies where key executives were recently employed by the audit firm, and created PCAOB oversight.
